plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Streets and plazas turn into tunnels of lavender-blue haze as thousands of trumpet-shaped flowers open in drooping clusters. When the blossoms fall, they leave soft purple carpets on the pavement below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in November (roughly October to December)
plants.funFact: Jacarandas are native to South America but now line streets across the world, from Buenos Aires to Pretoria to Sydney. Their flowers often appear before the fern-like leaves fully emerge, which makes the display look even more dramatic.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum lavandulifolium
plants.description: This tough, bushy wild daisy covers itself in small golden button-like flower heads just as autumn fades. Its finely cut, aromatic leaves and cheerful yellow blooms brighten roadsides and hillsides when little else is flowering.
plants.location: Eastern Asia, including China, Korea and Japan
plants.funFact: Wild chrysanthemums like this one are close relatives of the ancestors of the showy garden chrysanthemums. Those have been bred in East Asia for over a thousand years and are the emblem of autumn and of the Japanese imperial family.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: While most shrubs are shutting down for winter, this glossy evergreen opens delicate, lightly scented, rose-like blooms with golden stamens at the centre. Petals drift down in showers of pink and white beneath the dark foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, with the main flush in early to mid November
plants.location: Cornwall, United Kingdom, and other temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are native to Japan. Their relative, Camellia sinensis, gives us tea, and the seeds of sasanqua are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil.
